If nothing remains to me except the choice between a defeated devil and a victorious devil, I choose the defeated one. I am irresistibly drawn toward the defeated.
I shudder with disgust when I hear the songs of triumph sung by the victorious righteous and read in the Book of Wisdom (5:4–5):
“The wicked will be astonished by the unexpected good fortune of the righteous.”
I would rather be among the defeated wicked than among the victorious righteous.
Since I know both of them—the victors and the defeated—to be equally wicked, the matter becomes clearer still.
The bestial atrocities of the defeated and the bestial revenge taken for those atrocities really do cancel each other out.
What remains is the misery of these wretched defeated people and the happiness of these triumphant victors.
Heidegger passes the test of the comeback with the grade “fully satisfactory” on both sides.
